slides.visual: Full-bleed photo of your agents at a closing, an open house or last year's event [Pedro: pick a real photo of your people]. reThought logo small, bottom corner, only on this slide.
slides.notes: "Buenos días, familia. Welcome. For the next two days, I'm not going to lecture you. You're going to write, talk, practice and leave with a plan you built with your own hands. If I'm doing most of the talking, call me on it." Point to the city: Milwaukee or Florida. Thank anyone who traveled.
slides.workbook: Opening p.1 (cover, no need to open yet)

slides.visual: Black screen, white type, green underline under "best."
slides.notes: Wait for people to stand. Then: "Stay standing if you can tell me exactly WHY it was your best year." Most will sit. "That's what these two days fix. A good year you can't explain is luck. A good year you can explain, you can repeat." Everyone sits. Ask one person still standing: "What was the reason?" Keep it to 30 seconds.

slides.onScreen: "Find a partner you don't sit with. 60 seconds."
slides.visual: Two coffee cups clinking, or two people shaking hands. Large green timer: 1:00.
slides.notes: "This person is your accountability partner for both days and for the first 30 days of 2027. You'll role play with them, check their math, and read their numbers every Friday. Pick someone who will hold you to it, not someone who will let you off easy." If the room is uneven, make one trio.
slides.activity: Pairs, standing, 1 min to find, 2 min to trade name, office, and "one thing I want from these two days."

slides.visual: Photo of a room of people reading together, or simply the number 2, huge, green.
slides.notes: "Open to page 2. We read these four together, out loud, like we mean it." Read in unison. Then: "Turn to your partner. Which one of the four is going to be hardest for YOU? Be honest." 60 seconds. Call on two pairs. Model it first: [Pedro: tell them which agreement is hardest for you, for example the phone one]. End with the room saying the closing line on the page together in Spanish.
slides.activity: Whole room reads aloud (1 min), pair share (1 min), two pairs report (1 min).

slides.visual: Three boxes left to right. Box 1 "Mind" and box 2 "Target" in green labeled Day 1. Box 3 "Machine" in navy labeled Day 2. Nothing else.
slides.notes: "Today we fix the lens first, then we set the target. Tomorrow we build the machine that hits it: social media, ads, buyers, listings. Most retreats skip the first box. We start there because the best plan in the world dies if your head says 'that won't work for me.'" Point to page 3 for the full list, do not read it.

slides.visual: Plain white, black type. Quotation marks in green.
slides.notes: Raise your own hand first. "I have. Every one of us has. In Puerto Rico, in Orlando, in Milwaukee, everybody thinks their market is the exception." Ask: "What else do we say? Give me another one." Take two or three from the room (expect "my clients don't do social media," "I tried ads").

slides.visual: Full-bleed macro photo of a single snowflake on black. (For Florida: "Yes, I know we don't get snow. Stay with me.")
slides.notes: Tell the origin story in your words: a farmer in the 1880s spent years photographing thousands of snowflakes under a microscope and never found two the same. That's where "you're one of a kind" comes from. "And it's true. You ARE one of a kind. Your story, your family, your clients. Here's the problem: we take that true thing and we turn it into a wall." Workbook p.5 has the three parts; don't read them.

slides.visual: Split screen. Left, navy: a brick wall. Right, green: an open door.
slides.notes: "Same agent, same market, same week. One says 'that won't work here' and it never gets tried. The other says 'let's see how it could work here' and runs it ten times. The wall costs you the listing you didn't call, the ad you didn't run." Ask: "Which side did you live on more in 2026?" Don't take answers; let it sit 5 seconds. Point to the swap table on p.5 as their reference.
slides.workbook: Open the Mind p.5 (the trap, the cost, the swap table)

slides.onScreen: "[Pedro: one word or photo from your story]"
slides.visual: A personal photo connected to a time you resisted something that later worked (for example, the first time you ran an ad, went live, or called an expired).
slides.notes: [Pedro: tell your own snowflake story. Structure: what you told yourself, why it felt realistic, what finally made you try it, what happened. 90 seconds max.] Close with: "As you listen, write down the one sentence from my story that hits you. Page 6, box 1."

slides.onScreen: "Page 6. Write it. Fold it. Seal it. 5 minutes."
slides.visual: A folded paper card with a green seal sticker. Timer 5:00.
slides.notes: "Box 2 is private. Nobody reads it but you. Write the sentence you tell yourself about why something won't work for you. If it starts with 'my market,' 'my clients' or 'I tried that,' you found it." Walk the room. Under the sentence, they write the open-mind question (use the swap table). Then fold. "We open these together at the very end of tomorrow." En español: "Sé honesto. Esto es solo para ti."
slides.activity: Individual, silent writing, 5 min. Fold the card.

slides.onScreen: "Results first. Opinions second. / Primero pruebas, después opinas."
slides.visual: Two stacked words, "Results" big in green, "Opinions" smaller in gray below.
slides.notes: "Here's the deal for two days. Everything you hear, you run as taught first. When you have results, then you adapt it to your style. Not before. Your opinion of an idea you haven't tried isn't data." Ask the room to say the Spanish line with you once.
slides.workbook: Open the Mind p.5 (the rule box, point only)

slides.onScreen: "Walk it up. Then tell your partner one thing."
slides.visual: Photo of a wooden box or envelope labeled "Día 2."
slides.notes: "Bring your folded card to the box up front." (Movement: everybody up.) When they're back: "Tell your partner one idea you're going to try in 2027 even if it feels like it's not for you." 1 minute each. Bridge: "Now let's look at what you already built this year and never turned on."
slides.activity: Whole room walks cards to the front box (2 min), pair share (2 min).
slides.workbook: Open the Mind p.6 (step 3, card folded)

slides.onScreen: "Did you choose them, or did they choose you?"
slides.visual: Photo of a front door with a hand knocking, split with a phone ringing.
slides.notes: "Think about your last ten closings. Not the money. The people. How did they get to you?" Don't explain F and R yet. Let them think 20 seconds.

slides.onScreen: "You built the car. Now drive it."
slides.visual: A new car in a garage under a cover, keys on the hood.
slides.notes: "2026 was a big setup year for us. [Pedro: name what reThought rolled out in 2026, for example Dashbrew smart lists, the Zero to 45 meeting, the monthly email.] Raise your hand if you set up something this year and haven't really used it since." Laugh with them. "2027 isn't about learning more. It's about using what's already in your garage, every week."

slides.onScreen: "Page 8. Box three is the gold. 4 minutes."
slides.visual: Three empty boxes, the third outlined in green.
slides.notes: "Systems you set up, skills you learned, and box three: what you built but don't use yet. Box three is where your 2027 starts. It's money already paid for." Walk the room and peek at box three lists.

slides.onScreen: "Page 8. Ten names. F or R. 5 minutes."
slides.visual: A large F and a large R, side by side, green and navy.
slides.notes: Explain in one breath: "F, you found them: a call, an open house, an ad, a door. R, they found you: a referral, a repeat, a sign call." Phones out: pull last 10 closings from Lofty. "First name and the deal. Circle one letter."
slides.activity: Individual, 5 min, phones allowed for this one.

slides.visual: A number line 0 to 10 across the screen, green dots.
slides.notes: Before the session, tape numbers 0 to 10 along the back wall or floor. "Go stand on the number of clients YOU found." Look at the shape of the room. Ask someone near 0 to 2: "How does it feel when the referrals slow down?" Ask someone near 7 to 10: "What's the one thing you do every week?" "Referrals are a blessing. I want more of them for all of you. But if all your business is R, somebody else decides when you get paid. Tomorrow builds your F side."
slides.activity: Whole room, standing line-up, 4 min, two interviews.
slides.workbook: Open the Mind p.8 (I found / they found me totals)

slides.visual: Your own number, huge, green.
slides.notes: [Pedro: share your own F/R split from your last 10 deals, or from the brokerage as a whole if you have it. What it taught you.] Keep it honest: if your number is mostly R, say so; it gives them permission.

slides.onScreen: "Which one gets switched on in January?"
slides.visual: A light switch, flipped to on, green.
slides.notes: "Read your box three to your partner. Then say which ONE you will run first in January. Circle it." Ask two people to share with the room. Bridge: "Now the real numbers. Nobody grades this book."

slides.visual: Car rear-view mirror with a sunrise road behind.
slides.notes: "Remember agreement number three. Real numbers. Nobody collects this book. A gap tells you where to aim. It doesn't tell you who you are. If you came up short in 2026, welcome to the club. So did I." Pull up Lofty now; 2026 numbers come from there before the move to Dashbrew.

slides.visual: A simple two-bar chart with YOUR real goal and actual [Pedro: insert your real 2026 goal and actual, GCI or closings].
slides.notes: [Pedro: walk your own scoreboard. Biggest gap, why it happened, what you'd do differently. 2 minutes.] "If I can put mine on a screen in front of all of you, you can write yours on a page nobody sees."

slides.onScreen: "Page 10. Goal. Actual. Gap. Circle the biggest. 6 minutes."
slides.visual: Three column headers, the third with a green circle drawn around it. Timer 6:00.
slides.notes: "Six numbers. If you didn't set a goal, write what you wanted in January. Circle the biggest gap: that row gets your attention in the plan." Then the bottom half: wins, lessons, keep, stop, start. "Write fast. Two or three each. Don't polish."

slides.onScreen: "One win. One stop. Tell your partner."
slides.visual: Thumbs up and a stop sign, side by side.
slides.notes: "Read one win and one thing you're stopping. Partner, your only job is to ask 'why?' once." After: "Star the one you'll act on first."

slides.visual: The number huge in green, small gray label: "sample page, sphere and past clients."
slides.notes: "This is from the sample on page 9. Sphere: $45,000 in GCI on $600 of cost. That's 75 dollars back for every dollar. The ad line on the same sample is 3 to 1. Not bad, but look at the difference. This isn't 'ads are bad.' Tomorrow we fix ads. It's 'know what each source pays you back.'" Ask: "Anybody want to guess their own sphere number?"
slides.workbook: Open the Mind p.9 (how the return works)

slides.visual: Zoom on a single filled row of the source table (made-up agent, sample numbers): Open houses · 3 closings · $21,000 GCI · $450 cost (signs, snacks, flyers) · return about 47 to 1. Draw the division as a big green fraction.
slides.notes: "Count the cost honest: money plus paid tools. Signs, coffee, the portal subscription. Then GCI divided by cost. If a source has closings and almost no cost, that's your foundation. If a source has cost and no closings, it's a leak." Do the division live on a phone so they see it's simple.

slides.onScreen: "Page 11. Every source. Divide. Pick two and one. 8 minutes."
slides.visual: Two green up arrows, one red scissors icon. Timer 8:00.
slides.notes: "Pull your Lofty source report. One row per source. Then choose two sources to double down on and one to cut or fix." Coach while walking: "If you don't know the cost, estimate and write 'est.'"

slides.visual: A judge's gavel, or a boxing glove, light and playful.
slides.notes: "Partner A, read your two and your one. Partner B, for each choice ask 'why that one?' The answer has to have a number in it. No 'I just feel like it.'" Switch after 2.5 min. Then: "Write the number next to each choice." Bridge to break: "After the break, you pick the number you want. And it starts with your life, not your GCI."

slides.visual: Coffee, café con leche, a pastelillo. Countdown timer.
slides.notes: Remind phones: "Check your calls now. When we're back, face down again."

slides.visual: Full-bleed photo of a family at a front door with keys (stock or one of your closings with written OK).
slides.notes: "Who do you do it for? Not 'I want to make more money.' Who changes if 2027 is your best year?" Give them 20 silent seconds. "Most business plans start with GCI. Ours starts with your life. The GCI comes after."

slides.visual: [Pedro: a photo of your family, your boys, or the thing your best year paid for.]
slides.notes: [Pedro: your story. What your best year changed for your family, your community and for you. Specific details: the trip, the team you sponsored, the moment you knew you ran a business, not a job. 2 minutes.] Close: "Specific is powerful. 'Comfortable' doesn't get you out of bed. 'A week in Rincón with my kids' does."
slides.workbook: Open the Mind p.12 (family, community, por mí)

slides.onScreen: "Page 13. Your closings. Who it changes. 3 minutes."
slides.visual: Three empty cards labeled with icons only: a house, a soccer ball, a mirror.
slides.notes: "Top of page 13. Write your 2027 closings next to your best year so far. Then fill the three boxes. Real names, real things." Walk the room. If someone writes "financial freedom," ask "What would that look like on a Tuesday?"

slides.visual: Zoom on the bottom of a made-up receipt (sample numbers): Needed after split $82,400 ÷ 0.75 = $109,867. Circle the 0.75 in green, cross out a "75" in red.
slides.notes: "Here's a made-up agent with a 75% split. Monthly budget $4,200 times 12, plus savings, plus taxes, plus business costs: $82,400 needed after split. Divide by 0.75. Not 75. That one decimal is the mistake I see every year." On taxes: "Ask your accountant. Don't guess low." (Workbook has the guideline.)
slides.workbook: Open the Mind p.12 to 13 (the receipt)

slides.onScreen: "Build your receipt. Partner runs the math. 8 minutes."
slides.visual: A paper receipt, long, curling. Timer 8:00.
slides.notes: 5 minutes to fill, 3 minutes to swap: "Your partner reads your receipt line by line and does the division on their phone. If you get different answers, find out why." Circulate with a calculator.

slides.visual: The number 5 filling half the screen, green. "a day" small underneath.
slides.notes: "On the sample page, a $142,857 year comes down to five conversations a day. Not five closings. Five conversations. A big year is built from a small day that you repeat 240 times." Ask: "How many of you had five real conversations about real estate yesterday?" Hands.

slides.visual: A five-rung ladder, labels only, no numbers. The bottom rung glows green.
slides.notes: Walk down the ladder: average GCI per side, how many agreements close (sample uses 80%), how many appointments become agreements (sample uses half), how many conversations it takes to get one appointment (sample uses 20), working days (240). "Use your own 2026 ratios if you have them. If you don't, use the sample and fix it in March." [Pedro: if you know the brokerage's real average GCI per side, say it here.]
slides.workbook: Open the Mind p.12 and p.14

slides.onScreen: "Page 14. Down the ladder. Then pick your three. 8 minutes."
slides.visual: The same ladder, now with blanks. Timer 8:00.
slides.notes: "Bring your GCI target from the receipt. One line at a time, each line uses the one above. Then split your closings across two or three primary sources, not ten, and name the weekly activity that feeds each one. Use the two sources you picked to double down on in the last block." Finish with "My 2027 on one line" at the bottom of the page.

slides.onScreen: "Stand up. Your year in one breath."
slides.visual: A microphone, or a person speaking with a fist raised.
slides.notes: "Everybody up. Face your partner. Say it like this: 'In 2027 I close [X], which is [Y] in GCI, which means [Z] conversations a day, mostly from [sources].' Partner, if they mumble, make them say it again." Then ask two volunteers to say it to the whole room. Applause. "Every page after this points back to that line."
slides.activity: Pairs, standing, 3 min. Two volunteers to the room.
slides.workbook: Open the Mind p.14 (my 2027 on one line)

slides.visual: A clock at 9:00 with a giant bite taken out of it.
slides.notes: "Turn to your partner. What usually steals your morning? Email, a showing request, a fire at a closing, the kids' school?" 1 minute. Take three answers. "Every one of those is real. That's why the lead gen block goes on the calendar FIRST, before anything else can claim the time."

slides.visual: A phone calendar screenshot with a green block every morning, Monday to Friday.
slides.notes: "Motivation is great at a retreat. On a rainy Tuesday in February, it's gone. What's left is what's on your calendar. Your five conversations a day become a block of time, same hours every working day."

slides.visual: [Pedro: a screenshot of your actual calendar, personal items blurred.]
slides.notes: [Pedro: walk your own week. When your prospecting or lead gen time is, what you protect, family time, the day it fell apart and how you got it back.] "If I can do it with a brokerage and two boys in basketball, you can protect two hours." [Pedro: adjust to your real life.]

slides.onScreen: "Page 15. Green first. Same hours, five days. 5 minutes."
slides.visual: A blank weekly grid with one green row lit across Monday to Friday. Timer 5:00.
slides.notes: "Color the lead gen block first, same time all five days. Then appointments, follow-up, family and rest. If you're a parent, block pickup. If Sunday is church and family, block it." Spanish nudge: "La familia también va en el calendario."

slides.visual: The phone "repeat every weekday" setting, zoomed.
slides.notes: Do it live with your phone on the screen (mirror it or show a screenshot sequence). "Create the event. Name it 'Lead gen: 5 conversations.' Repeat every weekday. Alert 10 minutes before. Then make a second one: Friday, 30 minutes, 'Score my week.'" Wait until every phone is done.
slides.workbook: Open the Mind p.15 to 16 (check boxes)

slides.visual: Two columns. Left: a sun icon with six small dots (the daily list). Right: a single Friday calendar icon with "30" on it.
slides.notes: "Left side, every working day, same order, it's on page 16. Right side, Friday, 30 minutes: write the week, compare to target, name one fix, text your partner, block next week." Show the sample fix on the page ("start at 8, not 9") as the kind of answer you want. Don't read the list.

slides.visual: A green block icon next to a plate. Playful.
slides.notes: "No green block, no lunch." Laugh. "Show your partner your phone. Same block all five days? Friday blocked? Partner, check the box on their page." Then the bridge: "This morning you set the target. The number needs a person. After lunch, you decide who that person is."
slides.workbook: Open the Mind p.16 (check boxes, next: Identity)

slides.visual: A table of food, warm light. Countdown.
slides.notes: "Sit with someone from another office at lunch."

slides.onScreen: "Who hits the number you wrote this morning?"
slides.visual: Full-bleed photo of a person looking in a mirror, slightly out of focus.
slides.notes: "This morning you wrote a number. Here's the hard truth: the 2026 version of you already had a chance at that number. Who do you have to BE in 2027 to hit it? What does that person do at 8 AM that you don't do today?" 30 seconds of silence.

slides.visual: An empty interview chair facing a desk, warm light.
slides.notes: "Imagine you're the broker, and you're hiring the agent who closes your 2027 number. What would you look for? How do they answer leads? What do they say no to?" Ask the room for three traits. Write them on a flip chart. "That's who we're writing today."

slides.visual: Zoom on one filled box (made-up agent): "I am the agent who... calls back every lead before 7 PM, even on game nights." Green underline under "calls back."
slides.notes: "Present tense. 'I am,' not 'I will try to.' Small, real, checkable. You can tell if this agent did it or not." Then point to the three-word sets on page 1. "Pick three that make you sit up a little straighter. Or write your own." [Pedro: say your own three words here.]

slides.visual: Four empty boxes, three blank lines below. Timer 7:00.
slides.notes: "One or two lines a box. Box 4, what you say no to, is the one most people skip. Don't. The line you hold protects your family time and your fee." Walk the room. Spanish nudge for anyone stuck on box 2: "¿Por quién te levantas temprano?"

slides.visual: A calendar page torn to Dec 31, confetti, a sunset.
slides.notes: [Pedro: read your own December 31, 2027 statement, past tense, with numbers, places and people: business, family, health, money. 45 seconds.] "Short and true wins. Mine isn't a speech. It's a promise I can check."

slides.onScreen: "Write next New Year's Eve. Past tense. 3 minutes."
slides.visual: Timer 3:00 over a blurred fireworks photo.
slides.notes: "It already happened. What's true? Numbers, places, people." Walk and look for anyone writing "I hope."
slides.workbook: Identity p.2 (what is true on Dec 31)

slides.onScreen: "Read it to your partner. Then find a quiet corner."
slides.visual: A phone voice memo screen, red record button.
slides.notes: "Read it out loud to your partner. Partner, one question: does it sound like them? If it sounds like a LinkedIn post, they rewrite one line." Then: "Get up, find a corner, the hallway, outside, and record yourself reading it. Voice memo. Come back in 3 minutes."
slides.activity: Pairs 2 min, then individual recording anywhere in the venue, 3 min.

slides.visual: An alarm clock at 7:00 next to a phone.
slides.notes: "Set the alarm now: 'Play my 2027.' Tomorrow morning, before you check email, you hear yourself say it." Bridge: "People hire the expert they see the most. Now we make this person visible."

slides.onScreen: "Why did your last client pick you?"
slides.visual: Two business cards side by side, identical, one with a handwritten note on it.
slides.notes: "Not 'because I'm good.' What did they actually say? Turn to your partner, 60 seconds." Take two answers. Listen for things like "you spoke Spanish," "you explained it," "you grew up here." "Notice nobody said 'because you sold 24 homes.' They picked a person."

slides.onScreen: "They can beat your numbers. Not your story."
slides.visual: A scoreboard with a bigger number on the other side, and a single family photo in front of it.
slides.notes: "There's always an agent who sold more. When you lead with a number, you invite the comparison. When you lead with a story nobody else can tell, the right people feel it was written for them." Point to the contrast on page 3, don't read it.

slides.visual: [Pedro: a real photo from where you come from: a street, a house, your family.]
slides.notes: [Pedro: tell your story in the five layers: where you come from, the turning point you won't accept again, what you believe that most agents won't say, how you talk off camera, the problem you fight and for whom. 2 minutes.] Then: "Your turn. And remember: your story, never a client's without a written OK."

slides.visual: Five layers of earth in a cross-section, deepest at the bottom glowing green.
slides.notes: "Dig deepest first. Origin. Mission comes last, because it grows out of the rest."

slides.onScreen: "Page 4. By hand. Phone face down. 10 minutes."
slides.visual: A pen on paper, coffee cup. Timer 10:00.
slides.notes: "Origin first, mission last. A turning point is not a confession. Write what you'd tell a client over coffee, not your therapist." At 7 minutes: "Start your one-line story at the bottom." (The page suggests 15 minutes; tell them to finish the layers tonight if they need more.)

slides.visual: A coffee cup on the left, a TV with an infomercial on the right.
slides.notes: "Say your one line to your partner. Partner, one word: coffee or commercial? If it sounds like a commercial, cut every word they stumbled on and say it again."

slides.visual: Four boxes in a row, icons: a person silhouette, a map pin, a key, a checkmark.
slides.notes: "Your story is the why. A stranger scrolling gives you five seconds and needs the what. Four parts, in order. Part four has to be something they can check. 'I really care' fails, because every agent says it." Fair Housing, said clearly: "A place, a price, a property, a situation. Never a type of person."

slides.visual: Two cards (made-up agents). Milwaukee card: "I help Bay View condo owners move up to a house without moving twice." Florida card: "I help Poinciana renters turn their rent into a payment they own." Under each, part 4 in small type: "proved by a written move plan" and "proved by a payment worksheet before we tour."
slides.notes: "Notice what's there: a place, a situation, a result in their words. Notice what's not: no 'luxury,' no 'dream,' no type of person." In Milwaukee lead with the Bay View card; in Florida lead with Poinciana.

slides.visual: The blank sentence frame with three underscores, large. Timer 6:00.
slides.notes: "Pull from your identity page and your story line. Fill the four parts, then write it in one breath." Walk the room and check for any Fair Housing slips.

slides.onScreen: "Post it. Walk the wall. Check the ones that stick."
slides.visual: A wall covered in sticky notes, a hand adding a green check.
slides.notes: "Write your sentence big on a sticky note, no name. Post it on the wall. Then walk. Read each sentence once, look away, and if you can say who and where, put a check on it." Afterward, read two with the most checks and ask the room why they worked. Back at seats, partners say each other's who and where.
slides.activity: Whole room gallery walk, 4 min; pairs 1 min.

slides.visual: A paint swatch fan, grayed out, next to a bold green map pin.
slides.notes: "Most agents start with the logo. It feels like progress. The build order on page 5 starts with your position. Colors only prove what you stand for."

slides.onScreen: "Who looked you up before they called?"
slides.visual: A phone in a hand, Instagram search bar with an agent's name typed.
slides.notes: "Hands up if you've looked up an agent, a contractor, a restaurant before you called. Everybody. Your clients do the same thing to you. Two places decide: your Instagram profile and your Google listing."

slides.visual: A stopwatch, huge, green.
slides.notes: "That's how long they give your profile before they decide to call or keep scrolling. That's what the page says, and you know it's true because you do it too."

slides.visual: Two made-up profile mockups side by side (not the workbook sample). Before: logo as profile photo, bio "Realtor 🏡✨ Living my best life | DM for info," five links. After: smiling face filling the circle, name field "Ana Torres | Kissimmee Homes," bio line 1 is a brand sentence, one trigger word, one link, three pinned covers readable.
slides.notes: "Which one would you call? Why?" Take two answers. "Everything that's different between these two is on the scorecard on page 8."

slides.onScreen: "Cover your name. Last nine posts. Mine or anyone's? 3 minutes."
slides.visual: A grid of nine squares, some marked M in green, some A in gray.
slides.notes: "Put your thumb over your name and face. Look at your last nine posts. Could any agent have posted it? Mark it A. Those go on your archive list." Laughs are fine here. [Pedro: run the test on your own grid first, on screen, if you're brave.]

slides.onScreen: "Swap phones. Score them out of 20. 5 minutes each."
slides.visual: Two phones crossing, a scorecard. Timer 5:00, then reset.
slides.notes: "Pair with someone outside your usual circle for this one. Open their profile. Score it honestly on page 8: zero missed, one partly, two nailed it. Then swap." Write the total on their page.
slides.activity: New pairs, 5 min each, 1 min to switch.

slides.onScreen: "Fix your weakest three. Right now. 7 minutes."
slides.visual: A wrench icon over a phone. Timer 7:00.
slides.notes: "Change the name field. Paste your brand sentence into bio line 1. Archive two A posts. Pin three. Don't wait for a new photo shoot; fix what you can fix today." Walk the room and help people with settings. Have a tech-friendly agent as a floater [Pedro: name a floater].

slides.visual: A map pin with a star rating under it.
slides.notes: "Page 7 has the four steps and the exact name format. Open your Google Business Profile. Is it yours? Is it named with reThought Real Estate? Is your sentence the description? If not, that's tonight." Practice the review ask out loud once in English and once in Spanish with your partner.
slides.activity: Individual check 1 min, pairs say the ask 1 min.
slides.workbook: Personal brand p.7 (Google, say it) and p.8 (Google checklist)

slides.visual: Three speech bubbles, sent checkmarks in green.
slides.notes: "Pick three past clients who loved working with you. Send the review ask right now, in their language. Show your partner the sent messages." Bridge: "Break. When we come back: what to actually post, and how to get known in person."
slides.workbook: Personal brand p.8 (asked three past clients)

slides.visual: Countdown over a coffee photo.
slides.notes: none.

slides.blockTitle: What you post, getting known locally
slides.visual: A phone with a "SOLD" tile and a row of heart reactions.
slides.notes: "Be honest. Who reacts? Shout it out." Expect: other agents, the lender, mom, tía. "Right. How many of them are selling this year? That post makes us feel good. It doesn't bring the next seller."

slides.blockTitle: What you post, getting known locally
slides.visual: Four short lines stacked, made-up sale. Milwaukee version: "1950s Cape Cod, West Allis · Old water stains scared buyers off · We got the dry-basement report up front · Three offers the first weekend." Florida version: "Pool home, Kissimmee · Green pool in the old photos · Cleaned it, reshot at golden hour · Under contract in a week."
slides.notes: "The home, the problem, what we did, the result. Who reacts to this one? The next seller with a basement, or the next seller with a green pool. That's who we want." No address, no price, no names without a written OK.

slides.blockTitle: What you post, getting known locally
slides.visual: Three equal columns and a small fourth slice labeled "10%."
slides.notes: "Three things every week, plus a little bit of you: your coffee, your gym, your kids' game. People follow people. Pick ONE area to own, where you live or already sell. We're not entertainers. We're the local expert." Fair Housing reminder: homes, prices, places, commute. Not schools, safety or who lives there. Formats and hooks come tomorrow.

slides.blockTitle: What you post, getting known locally
slides.onScreen: "Page 10. One sale. Four lines. One area. 6 minutes."
slides.visual: Four empty lines, a map pin. Timer 6:00.
slides.notes: "Pick a sale you're proud of. Then pick your area and write why that one. Look at the five video ideas on the page. Those are tomorrow's homework." New agents: use a deal you helped on, or a home you toured.

slides.blockTitle: What you post, getting known locally
slides.visual: A phone ringing, green.
slides.notes: "Partner reads your story and tells you the challenge in one line. Then: if you were the next seller, would you call?"

slides.blockTitle: What you post, getting known locally
slides.visual: Full-bleed photo of an agent at a café counter, barista smiling, laptop open.
slides.notes: "Online gets you found. Offline gets you trusted. Two ways: borrow credibility from partners, a lender, an inspector, a local owner, and earn your own by being a regular somewhere, same spot, same time every week." Ask the one question from page 11 out loud: would your best future client be impressed if this played in their neighbor's house? RESPA: costs split by real use, nothing given for referrals.

slides.blockTitle: What you post, getting known locally
slides.visual: [Pedro: a photo of you with a real partner: a lender live, a client party, a business spotlight.]
slides.notes: [Pedro: tell one real partnership that brought you business or trust. What you did, how often, what came from it.] Then: "And tag your VIPs in Dashbrew when your contacts land in January: anyone who ever sent you a client."

slides.blockTitle: What you post, getting known locally
slides.onScreen: "Page 12. Two partners. Real dates. Text them now. 7 minutes."
slides.visual: A calendar with two dates circled in green, a phone with "sent."
slides.notes: "Not 'someday.' A date. Pick two partners and one client party. Your spot and your time. Count your VIPs today. Then text both partners before you leave this room: 'I want to do a weekly live with you starting January. Coffee next week?'" [Pedro: offer your own text wording in Spanish too, for example: "Quiero hacer un live semanal contigo empezando en enero. ¿Un café la semana que viene?"]

slides.blockTitle: What you post, getting known locally
slides.visual: Two phones side by side, both showing "Delivered."
slides.notes: "Partner, you hold them to the first date. Write it in your own calendar too." Bridge: "You know who you are and the market can see it. Every person you meet now needs a next step. That's Seguimiento."

slides.blockTitle: Seguimiento: your people, stages and rhythm
slides.visual: Section cover photo style: an agent on the phone, smiling, a coffee and a printed list.
slides.notes: "Seguimiento. Follow-up. This is training, not autopilot. Dashbrew holds the list. You make the calls." Say the slide line in Spanish, then in English: "The fortune is in the follow-up."

slides.blockTitle: Seguimiento: your people, stages and rhythm
slides.onScreen: "Who in your phone should have been your client?"
slides.visual: A phone contact list with one name highlighted, a "Sold" sign blurred in the background.
slides.notes: "Think of one person. They talked to you, they were interested, and then you saw them post their keys with another agent. Tell your partner that story in 60 seconds." Everybody has one.

slides.blockTitle: Seguimiento: your people, stages and rhythm
slides.visual: [Pedro: a photo that cues the story, for example a street or a house.]
slides.notes: [Pedro: your own lost-to-silence story. What happened, what it cost, what you changed.] "They didn't pick the other agent because the other agent was better. They picked the one who called."

slides.blockTitle: Seguimiento: your people, stages and rhythm
slides.visual: Two dials. Left dial: a clock face with stage names as small ticks. Right dial: three concentric circles (inner, middle, outer).
slides.notes: "Every contact gets one stage. It changes as they move. Past clients and sphere also get a circle. Together they tell you who to call and how often. Trash is only for fakes and duplicates. Everybody else stays." Point to page 1 for the stages and page 3 for the rhythm; don't read them. Walk the four rules at the bottom of page 3 in your own words, especially "people leap": a C can become an A tomorrow.

slides.blockTitle: Seguimiento: your people, stages and rhythm
slides.visual: A moving truck icon labeled "Lofty" driving to a house labeled "Dashbrew."
slides.notes: "In January your contacts move from Lofty to Dashbrew. Don't dump them in and walk away. Page 2: three passes, one evening, and every contact has a home." [Pedro: confirm the exact migration date and who supports agents on that night.] Practice the re-intro text once in English, once in Spanish, out loud with your partner.
slides.activity: Pairs say the re-intro text, 1 min.

slides.blockTitle: Seguimiento: your people, stages and rhythm
slides.onScreen: "Trade phones. Five contacts. Stage and circle, out loud. 4 minutes."
slides.visual: Two phones crossing, five dots.
slides.notes: "Your partner scrolls your contacts or Lofty and picks five names. You say the stage, the circle if they're sphere or past client, and the next date. Can't answer? That's the point. That's what January fixes."

slides.blockTitle: Seguimiento: your people, stages and rhythm
slides.onScreen: "Stand. Two lines. Five seconds per answer."
slides.visual: A stopwatch at 0:05, two arrows facing each other.
slides.notes: Have everyone stand in two facing lines with page 4. Line A reads one of the six answers (or a real one from their own week). Line B says the stage and the next touch in five seconds, answer key covered. After three answers, line B shifts one person left. Switch roles halfway. Pedro calls time with a bell. Debrief: "Which one did you get wrong most?" Usually "bought with another agent" and "maybe next year."
slides.activity: Whole room, standing lines, 10 min, 2 min debrief.

slides.blockTitle: Seguimiento: your people, stages and rhythm
slides.visual: A phone call ending screen vs. a calendar invite being created.
slides.notes: "Every answer gets a next step on the calendar before you dial the next number. Log it, update the stage, add a note, set the date. Four moves." Role play the "glad you have someone" line from page 4 in Spanish with a volunteer: "Si algo cambia, llámeme." Keep it warm. "They bought with someone else? They still get the monthly touch. Silence isn't a no."

slides.blockTitle: Seguimiento: your people, stages and rhythm
slides.visual: A January calendar, one evening circled in green.
slides.notes: "Put it in your phone now: the evening in January you sort everyone. Tell your partner the date. Partner, put a reminder to text them that night." Bridge: "Now: what you do when they don't answer."

slides.blockTitle: The first 7 days, then never stop
slides.onScreen: "New lead. How fast do you call?"
slides.visual: Four big options on screen: "5 min · 1 hour · Same day · Tomorrow."
slides.notes: "Hands up, honestly. Five minutes? An hour? Same day? Tomorrow?" Count. "No judgment. But think about the last time you filled out a form online. How long until you forgot you did it?"

slides.blockTitle: The first 7 days, then never stop
slides.visual: "30" huge in green on the left, "3" small in gray on the right.
slides.notes: "About thirty personal touches in four months. That's our plan. Most agents stop after three. That gap between thirty and three is your business." (Both numbers are on page 5.)

slides.blockTitle: The first 7 days, then never stop
slides.visual: Seven dots in a row. The first three are big and green with three small marks under each, the last four are smaller and navy with one mark each. A long gray arrow continues after day 7 labeled "never stop."
slides.notes: "Three touches a day for three days. One call a day to day 7, each at a different time. Then slow down, never stop. What counts: calls, texts, video texts, voicemails, your own DMs. What doesn't: emails and automatic messages. No voicemail until the fourth call. And if they answer, stop the plan and run the call." Point to page 5 for the full grid.

slides.blockTitle: The first 7 days, then never stop
slides.visual: A phone with a green "calling" screen.
slides.notes: Ask for a volunteer to play Maria, an ad lead who asked for the buying guide three minutes ago. Pedro runs call 1 out loud, then the "they called, you missed it" text. Then do it again in Spanish with a Spanish-speaking volunteer. Debrief: "What did you notice? One question, short, no 'how are you.'" [Pedro: or play a real recording of one of your calls, with permission.]
slides.activity: Pedro and volunteer in front of the room, 3 min.

slides.blockTitle: The first 7 days, then never stop
slides.onScreen: "Page 6. Eight touches. Out loud. Make them yours. 10 minutes."
slides.visual: Eight small speech bubbles in two rows. Timer 10:00.
slides.notes: "Take turns reading them out loud with your partner, in whichever language you'll use. Change the words until they sound like you. Keep the move: short, one question, one ask." Walk and listen. Coach anyone reading in a robot voice.

slides.blockTitle: The first 7 days, then never stop
slides.visual: The phrase in a red circle with a slash through it.
slides.notes: "From today, every time someone in this room says 'just checking in,' they owe the office a dollar for the coffee fund." [Pedro: decide if you want to run this as a real office rule.] "Every touch gives something: a home, a number, a question."

slides.blockTitle: The first 7 days, then never stop
slides.onScreen: "Write your opener. Say it three times."
slides.visual: A pen and a blank line. Timer 3:00.
slides.notes: "At the bottom of page 6, your first-call opener in your words. Then say it out loud three times to your partner. Third time should sound like you're not reading."

slides.blockTitle: The first 7 days, then never stop
slides.onScreen: "Ten minutes. Every day. Thirty days. When?"
slides.visual: A calendar grid with 30 small green checkmarks.
slides.notes: "Your partner is your role-play partner for the first 30 days of 2027. Ten minutes a day. Pick the time now and put it in both phones. Who calls who?" Bridge: "Next: staying present with everybody, even when nobody is moving."

slides.onScreen: "What did a business send you that you actually liked?"
slides.visual: An open mailbox with a handwritten envelope.
slides.notes: "Think of something a business sent you that you were glad to get. A card from your dentist, a reminder from your mechanic, a pie." Take two answers. "What made it good? It was about you, not them."

slides.visual: Four weekly icons in a row: a chart, a question mark, a house, a map pin. "Wk 1 · Wk 2 · Wk 3 · Wk 4" under them.
slides.notes: "Four emails a month to everyone. reThought writes them, you make them yours in ten minutes, Dashbrew sends them." [Pedro: confirm the date the drafts arrive each month and who to call if one is wrong.] "Then the important part: the people who raise their hand. Saved a home, asked for a value, clicked twice. Dashbrew flags them on your morning list. Call about what they did, never 'I saw you opened my email.'"

slides.onScreen: "Hand raiser alert. Call her. 60 seconds each."
slides.visual: A heart icon on a listing photo.
slides.notes: "Partner A is the client who just saved a home in Dashbrew. Partner B calls. One question, two options. Then switch, and do round two in Spanish." Use the say-it lines on page 7 as a starting point, not a script to read.

slides.visual: Five envelope icons with one open; a row of 100 dots with one green.
slides.notes: "That's the score to expect from the monthly emails. Lower than that? Tell us and we fix the subject lines. You don't need everybody to click. You need to call the one who does."

slides.visual: A 12-month strip, a few months filled with icons (a pie, a card, a cookout). Timer 6:00.
slides.notes: "Your area, your follow-up day, your personal line. Then one useful touch per month and who gets it. Then swap with your partner: any month that's 'just checking in' gets rewritten. Read each one as the client: would you be glad to get it?"

slides.visual: A list of four colored bars in order, a downward arrow, and a big "0" at the bottom.
slides.notes: "One hour of follow-up and one hour of new conversations every working day, before email. Same order: clients first, then inbox and missed calls, then the plan, then extra. A new lead never waits behind an old one." Mention the Friday self-audit: anyone untouched in five days gets touched before the weekend.

slides.visual: Ten chairs at a table, eight filled, two empty.
slides.notes: "Out of every ten appointments you book, eight should actually happen. Booked is not done. A no-show is a reschedule, not a loss." Have the room say the reschedule line in Spanish together once, from page 9.

slides.visual: A made-up funnel (sample numbers): Leads 220 → Conversations 90 (41%) → Set 36 (40%) → Held 27 (75%) → Signed 14 (52%) → Closed 11 (79%). The 40% is circled in green.
slides.notes: "Kept equals this row divided by the row above. This made-up agent's leak is conversations to appointments set. The fix for that leak is in the table on page 10: the first call and 10 minutes of role play a day. Find yours."

slides.visual: A dripping faucet. Timer 6:00.
slides.notes: "Pull your 2026 counts from Lofty before it closes. Do the math. The lowest percent is your Q1 project." New agents: "No 2026 numbers? Your Q1 fix is speed: every lead called in five minutes." Then partner reads your math back.

slides.visual: A circular arrow made of house keys.
slides.notes: "Page 11 is the whole section on one page. Find any person on it and you know what to do next. 'Not yet' means the middle, not the trash. And closed isn't the end. Your past clients send the next one back to the top." Ask: "Where on the map are most of your contacts sitting right now?"

slides.visual: A green wrench icon.
slides.notes: "Tell your partner your biggest leak and the one fix for Q1. One sentence."
slides.workbook: Seguimiento p.10 (my one fix for Q1)

slides.onScreen: "What did you do today for the first time?"
slides.visual: A sunrise over a road, warm.
slides.notes: "Go around your table. One sentence each: something you did today that you've never done. Built a ladder, sent the review texts, said your story out loud." Then ask two tables to share their favorite. Celebrate.

slides.visual: Three icons: headphones, a phone, a question mark.
slides.notes: "Three things tonight. One: tomorrow at 7 AM your alarm plays your December 31 recording. Two: say your first-call opener three times on the drive. Three: bring one real question a client asked you this month. We turn it into a video tomorrow morning." Partners: "Tell each other which one you'll do first."
slides.workbook: Identity p.2, Seguimiento p.6, Social media p.6 (preview)

slides.visual: Group photo moment: [Pedro: take a live group photo right now, then put it on the first slide of Day 2].
slides.notes: "Today you opened your mind and set the target. Tomorrow we install the machine that hits it, starting with your phone. Get some rest." Take the group photo.

slides.visual: The live group photo you took at the end of Day 1, full-bleed.
slides.notes: "Buenos días. Hands up if your alarm played your December 31 recording this morning. Keep it up if you listened to the whole thing." Celebrate whoever did. "Yesterday was about knowing. Today is about doing."

slides.visual: A phone screen with a green calendar block and a "Delivered" text bubble.
slides.notes: "Show your partner one thing you actually did since yesterday: the repeating lead gen block, the review texts, the partner text, the recording. Proof, not promises. Then tell them the client question you brought for this morning." Ask two pairs to share what their partner did.
slides.workbook: Open the Mind p.15 to 16, Personal brand p.8 and 12

slides.visual: Four boxes left to right with a thin green line connecting them, like a pipe. Small "card" icon at the very end.
slides.notes: "Yesterday you set the target. Today we install the machine that hits it. First your phone: social media. Then El motor: the ads that bring strangers to you. Then what you say to a buyer and a seller once they're on the phone. And at the very end, we open the cards you sealed yesterday." Ask partners: "Which of these four do you need most? Tell your partner." 1 minute.

slides.blockTitle: Earn the attention, the format menu
slides.onScreen: "Instagram deletes you tonight. Who can you still call?"
slides.visual: A phone with an "Account disabled" screen.
slides.notes: "It happens. Hacked, flagged, closed. If that happened tonight, how many of your followers could you actually call tomorrow? Tell your partner a rough number." Take two. "That's the difference between an audience and a database."

slides.blockTitle: Earn the attention, the format menu
slides.visual: Left: apartment keys on a rental tag. Right: house keys with a Dashbrew-green keychain.
slides.notes: "Followers are rented. The app decides who sees you and can change the rules tomorrow. A name and number in Dashbrew is yours, for years. So every post has one job: start a conversation that ends up in Dashbrew."

slides.blockTitle: Earn the attention, the format menu
slides.visual: Four icons connected by green arrows: a play button, a speech bubble, two speech bubbles, a contact card.
slides.notes: "That's the whole game. We'll come back to the last two steps before the break."

slides.blockTitle: Earn the attention, the format menu
slides.onScreen: "Page 2. One home base. How much Spanish?"
slides.visual: A phone showing Instagram, with smaller Facebook and YouTube icons orbiting it.
slides.notes: "One video, three places. Instagram is home base. You don't need TikTok and LinkedIn unless you love them. And for us, bilingual matters: it's the same idea in two posts, not subtitles. reKo drafts the Spanish, you fix it so it sounds like you, not like a translator." Fill the bottom of page 2: home base, cross-post, languages, Spanish posts per week.

slides.blockTitle: Earn the attention, the format menu
slides.visual: Left, in red, a made-up post: "PRICES ARE ABOUT TO EXPLODE. BUY NOW!!!" Right, in green, a made-up post: "Three homes sold on my street this month. Here's what they got."
slides.notes: "The feed rewards emotion more than truth. Fear and fake urgency get views and lose trust. We earn attention. We never hijack it." Ask: "Which one would your grandmother believe?" Point to the table on page 2.

slides.blockTitle: Earn the attention, the format menu
slides.onScreen: "Your last post. Four questions. Partner judges. 4 minutes."
slides.visual: Four checkboxes.
slides.notes: "Open your last post. Your partner looks at it and answers the four questions at the bottom of page 2. Any no means rewrite or kill it." Tonight they run their last three through it.

slides.blockTitle: Earn the attention, the format menu
slides.visual: Three blocks stacking like Legos, the third one green.
slides.notes: "A topic says what it's about. A format says how they watch it. Tension gives them a reason to stay to the end: a mistake, a surprise, a risk, a change. If a post flopped, don't change the topic. Change the format." Everything you post uses real numbers: your sales, your Dashbrew pages.

slides.blockTitle: Earn the attention, the format menu
slides.visual: A made-up topic card "HOA fees" with an arrow to a rebuilt hook: "Everyone says run from HOAs. Here's when I tell buyers to pick one." Second card for Milwaukee: "Property tax bill" to "If you're fighting your assessment without this, stop."
slides.notes: "HOA fees, flat. Add myth plus surprise and suddenly people want to know when you'd pick one. Notice the second one: a mistake plus a cost. Same topic, different door in." Ask the room: "What format did I use on each?"

slides.blockTitle: Earn the attention, the format menu
slides.onScreen: "A topic that flopped. New format. New tension. 6 minutes."
slides.visual: A sad emoji turning into a fire emoji. Timer 6:00.
slides.notes: "Pick a post that got nothing, or the client question you brought. With your partner, rebuild it two ways using the menu on page 4. Write the hook." Then ask three pairs to read their best one to the room. Applause for the boldest.

slides.blockTitle: Earn the attention, the format menu
slides.visual: A restaurant menu with three items circled in green marker.
slides.notes: "Twelve formats, each one does one job: reach, proof, saves, loyalty. Don't invent new ones. Circle three you'll rotate in January." Memes rule: one or two a week, the joke is on you or the job, never a client, a home or a group of people. [Pedro: show one meme you posted that worked, if you have one.]

slides.blockTitle: Earn the attention, the format menu
slides.onScreen: "Tonight: your last three posts, four questions."
slides.visual: Three post thumbnails with question marks.
slides.notes: "Write it at the top of page 3 so you remember. Now: tell your partner which of your three formats you're most nervous to try, and why." Bridge: "Every format lives or dies in the first few seconds. Let's write hooks."

slides.visual: A thumb mid-scroll over a phone, motion blur.
slides.notes: "That's how long you get before the thumb moves. The first three seconds decide if anyone hears the rest."

slides.visual: [Pedro: play the first 3 to 5 seconds of a real reel, one of yours or an agent's with permission, then pause.]
slides.notes: Pause after three seconds. "Thumbs up if you'd keep watching. Why? What did the first line do?" Then play the rest. "Notice: one line that opens a question, three short local points, one word to comment."

slides.visual: A timeline bar: 0:03 "Grab," 0:45 "Give," 0:60 "Ask." Green tick at each.
slides.notes: "Grab: one line that opens a question. Give: three points, short, specific, local. Ask: one word, like 'comment PLAN.' Every video, under a minute." The five starter hooks on page 5 are ready to use tomorrow.

slides.visual: Topic "closing costs" at the top. Three made-up hooks below: "Unpopular opinion: closing costs aren't the scary part." / "Everyone says the seller pays closing costs. Not always." / "I almost lost a buyer at the closing table over this."
slides.notes: "Hot take. Myth. Story. Same topic. Which one would make YOUR client stop?" Hands for each. "There's no right answer. That's why you write ten."

slides.onScreen: "Page 6. Your client's question. Ten hooks. Ten minutes. No judging."
slides.visual: A list of ten empty lines. Timer 10:00.
slides.notes: "Use the question you brought from a real client this month. Write one hook for each of the ten types. Don't judge, don't polish. Bad hooks are part of finding good ones." At 8 minutes: "Circle your two best."

slides.onScreen: "Score your best one with your partner. Out loud."
slides.visual: The number 35 with a dial; green zone above 28.
slides.notes: "Score it on the seven lines. 28 or more, you film it. 22 to 27, fix the weakest line. Under 22, change the format." Partners score each other's out loud.

slides.onScreen: "Post your hook. Three dots each. Vote."
slides.visual: Wall of sticky notes with green dot stickers.
slides.notes: "Write your winning hook big on a sticky. Post it on the hook wall. Everyone gets three dots. Vote for the hooks that would stop YOU." Read the top three out loud. Ask the writers what format they used.
slides.activity: Whole room gallery, 5 min; 2 min to read winners.

slides.onScreen: "Film it before lunch ends. Partner holds the phone."
slides.visual: A phone on a tripod, red record dot.
slides.notes: "Pick the spot now: hallway, outside, by the window, with the light on your face, not behind you. Your partner films you during lunch. One take is fine. It's episode zero." [Pedro: set up one simple filming corner with a ring light if possible.] Bridge: "Now: how to make this every week without panic."
slides.activity: Pairs plan their filming spot and time, 3 min.

slides.visual: Three options: "Daily panic · Once a week · When I remember."
slides.notes: Hands for each. Laugh. "If the answer is panic, it's because thinking and doing are happening at the same time."

slides.visual: Five stations as a factory line with day labels above: Mon, Mon, Tue, Wed, Wed.
slides.notes: "One idea a week, six posts. Monday you think, Tuesday you film everything in one session, Wednesday you edit and schedule. reKo, the second brain in Dashbrew, already knows your sentence, your client, your area and your voice. It does the first 80%. You add the 20% that only you can: your story, your opinion, the local detail. Check every fact." [Pedro: show a 30-second screen of reKo drafting your week, if you can.] Minimum standard is on page 7.

slides.visual: Three reel covers in the same template, made-up show "Rent vs. Own Friday," episodes 1, 2, 3 with different home photos.
slides.notes: "Same name, same day, same opening line. People start to expect it. A made-up example: 'Rent vs. Own Friday. This week: what $1,800 a month gets you.'" In Milwaukee, swap in a neighborhood show idea. [Pedro: if you have your own show, show it instead.]

slides.onScreen: "Page 8. Name your show. Write the opening line. 6 minutes."
slides.visual: A clapperboard with a blank title. Timer 6:00.
slides.notes: "Show name, day, the same opening line, words you always use, words you never use. Then read only your opening line to your partner. Can they guess the show?" Words you never use should include the Fair Housing and hype words from page 2.

slides.visual: A horizontal timeline with five dots: −15, 0, 10, 20, 60.
slides.notes: "The app shows your post to a few people first. If they react, it shows more. So you block the hour like an appointment: warm up by commenting on local accounts, post, send it to five people it actually helps, share it to Stories with a poll, answer every comment with a question." Clarify: "This hour is you, by hand. ManyChat is for ad keywords, that's El motor."

slides.onScreen: "A comment came in. Get the number in three replies."
slides.visual: A comment bubble: "How much do I need to buy?"
slides.notes: "Partner A comments as a follower. Partner B replies with a question, moves it to DM, asks for the best number to send the plan. Three messages max. Then switch, and do round two in Spanish." Debrief: "What did the best reply have in common?" (It ended with a question.)

slides.visual: A pile of heart icons on one side, a set of keys on the other.
slides.notes: "Every post moves somebody one step up the ladder: follower, conversation, contact, consult, client. Every Friday you write four numbers. Views and likes stay off the board." Point to the sample board on page 10: many conversations, few contacts means ask for the number sooner.

slides.visual: A phone with a Friday reminder notification.
slides.notes: "Set the Friday reminder. Same time as your weekly score from yesterday. Partner checks your board every Friday for the first month." Bridge: "Organic shows you what works. After the break, El motor: we pay to put your best stuff in front of the right people."

slides.visual: Countdown over a café photo.
slides.notes: "If you have five minutes, film your hook now."

slides.blockTitle: El motor: the machine and the kit
slides.visual: A dark living room lit only by a phone screen, a person on a couch.
slides.notes: "Somewhere in your area right now, someone is doing rent math on their phone. El motor is how that stranger ends up on the phone with you tomorrow at 9 AM. Referrals are luck you wait for. This is luck you build."

slides.blockTitle: El motor: the machine and the kit
slides.visual: Three boxes. Small icons: an eye, a magnet, a handshake.
slides.notes: "Attention: the avatar shapes the content and the ads find the people. Capture: ManyChat collects the contact and sends the guide. Conversion: Dashbrew alerts you, you call, Seguimiento takes over, the scoreboard tells you what to fix. Always in that order." Point to page 1 for the eight parts.

slides.blockTitle: El motor: the machine and the kit
slides.visual: [Pedro: a screenshot of your own Meta ads results from your "Realtor Pedro Bando Rivera" page, or one real number, big.]
slides.notes: [Pedro: tell your real ads story. What you tried first, what didn't work, what changed, what one appointment costs you now. Use only your real numbers.]

slides.blockTitle: El motor: the machine and the kit
slides.onScreen: "Page 2. Check what you have. Date the rest. 6 minutes."
slides.visual: A checklist with some green checks and some blank date lines. Timer 6:00.
slides.notes: "Every item gets a check or a 'ready by' date. Then your monthly ad budget, about 10% of the GCI you want, and the date your machine goes live." Remind: Housing category on every ad, every time. ManyChat asks consent before collecting contact info.

slides.blockTitle: El motor: the machine and the kit
slides.visual: A puzzle with one piece out.
slides.notes: "Partner reads your kit and asks one question: what's missing? Tonight, log in to every tool and confirm you can get in." [Pedro: name who in the office helps agents set up Meta Ads Manager and ManyChat.]

slides.onScreen: "What keeps your buyer up at 11 PM?"
slides.visual: A ceiling, dark, seen from a bed.
slides.notes: "Not 'they want a house.' What's the thought at 11 PM? Tell your partner in your client's words, not yours." Take three answers. Listen for "my rent went up again," "I don't know if my credit is good enough."

slides.visual: Left: a megaphone pointed at a stadium crowd. Right: one person on a couch looking at their phone, nodding.
slides.notes: "When an ad tries to fit everybody, nobody feels it was written for them. Describe one situation exactly and thousands of people who live it think 'that's me.' Situations keep you Fair Housing safe: renting, relocating, outgrowing, downsizing. Never age, family, religion or background."

slides.visual: Two made-up avatar cards. Milwaukee: 11 PM "looking at duplexes, wondering if upstairs rent covers the mortgage" · tried "asked a friend who said wait" · afraid "they're not 'investor' material" · hook: "Your upstairs tenant could pay half your mortgage. Here's how it works." Florida: 11 PM "checking their credit score again" · tried "an online calculator that said no" · afraid "their credit will keep them renting forever" · hook: "Think your credit's too low to buy in Kissimmee? Let's actually check."
slides.notes: "Q3, the thing they're afraid to say out loud, becomes the hook. Said kindly. One fear in three places: the ad, the DM, the call."

slides.onScreen: "Page 4. Answer as your client. The fear becomes the hook. 6 minutes."
slides.visual: Three question marks, the third in green. Timer 6:00.
slides.notes: "Write in their words, not yours. Then read your hook to your partner. If they don't say 'that's me' or 'I know someone like that,' rewrite Q3."

slides.visual: Two funnels: left one leaking from holes, right one sealed with a phone at the bottom.
slides.notes: Tell the story from page 5 in your own words: an agent boosted posts and ran a free home value form, got leads and not one client. Six months later, same budget, three campaigns, one avatar, one promise, a call in five minutes, and clients. [Pedro: if you have your own version of this story, tell yours instead.]

slides.visual: Three thermometer icons, blue to orange to red.
slides.notes: "Cold earns attention from anyone in your area, and Meta remembers who watched. Warm turns watchers into leads. Retarget books the call with people who engaged but haven't booked. Most of the budget goes to Warm. On day 7, move most of it to the ad with the cheaper booked appointment." All on page 5.

slides.onScreen: "Page 6. Three lines break the rules. Fix them. Tables race. 6 minutes."
slides.visual: Three red-flagged ad lines with a stopwatch.
slides.notes: "Housing ads can only target a location. Your words do the targeting: name the situation and the place, then promise one thing. Each table rewrites the three lines on page 6. First table to stand up with three clean rewrites reads them to the room. The room hunts for any word that describes who should live there." Then pairs trade and hunt in their own lines.
slides.activity: Tables 6 min, winning table stands and reads 2 min, pairs trade 2 min.

slides.onScreen: "Read it like Fair Housing is listening."
slides.visual: A person in a suit with a clipboard, friendly.
slides.notes: "Out loud, one line, to your partner, as if an officer were in the room. If you flinch at any word, it goes." Bridge: "Now: what happens the second someone comments."

slides.onScreen: "It answers at 2 AM. You call at 8."
slides.visual: A phone on a nightstand lighting up with a DM notification, clock reading 2:07.
slides.notes: "ManyChat watches for the word, sends the guide and hands the lead to Dashbrew. You set it up once. But it's not a touch. Your first 7 days start when YOU call."

slides.visual: Five icons in a row ending in a person with a phone, green.
slides.notes: "The word matches the caption exactly. First DM always has a button. Short. Test it from another account before the ad goes live." Details on page 7.

slides.onScreen: "Page 8. Your word. Your first DM. Your 48-hour question. 4 minutes."
slides.visual: A DM screen with blanks.
slides.notes: "Write your comment word, what the guide promises, the first DM, and the 48-hour question. Seller ads: the magnet is the do-it-yourself prep checklist. Give it freely." Fee wording in writing, before they sign.

slides.visual: A stopwatch next to a DM bubble.
slides.notes: "If your partner's ManyChat is live, comment their word on their post and time it. If it's not, paper test: you comment, they read their first DM out loud. Is it one line and a button?"

slides.visual: Two chairs at a table, one person sitting, versus a pile of mouse-click icons.
slides.notes: "Leads feel good. Appointments held are the score. Every Friday you fill one column on page 9, and the cost of each held appointment tells you what to fix." Show the four "low" boxes at the bottom of page 9.

slides.visual: The four words in the four corners of the screen, matching signs in the four corners of the room.
slides.notes: Before the session, post signs in the four corners. Read made-up scenarios; everyone walks to the corner with the fix: "Lots of views, almost no comments." (Hook.) "Plenty of comments, few leads land in Dashbrew." (Word and first DM.) "Leads land, but half were called the next day." (Speed.) "Appointments set, but half don't show." (Confirm text and call the day before.) Do four or five scenarios. Ask one person per corner to explain why.

slides.onScreen: "Live by ____. Partner reads the number Fridays."
slides.visual: A calendar with one date circled, a green "GO."
slides.notes: "Write the date your machine goes live. Your partner reads your cost per appointment held every Friday for the first month." Lunch instructions: "Film your hook if you haven't. Partner holds the phone."
slides.workbook: El motor p.2 and p.9 (check it)

slides.visual: Food on a table, a phone on a tripod in the corner.
slides.notes: "Filming corner is open." [Pedro: optional: post the best three hook videos on screen when everyone is back.]

slides.blockTitle: The buyer path and the first call
slides.onScreen: "What does a buyer actually need from you?"
slides.visual: A phone full of saved listing hearts, dozens of them.
slides.notes: (If you're showing lunch hook videos, play three, 2 min total, then this.) "Shout it out." Take answers. "Most of you said homes. They have Zillow. They have more homes than they can see. What they don't have is a plan."

slides.blockTitle: The buyer path and the first call
slides.visual: The number 45 huge, a key icon inside the 5.
slides.notes: "From first click to keys in 45 days. Same steps, every buyer, every time."

slides.blockTitle: The buyer path and the first call
slides.visual: Eight small numbered dots on a path, a lock icon between dot 4 and dot 5.
slides.notes: "Each step has a finish line. You don't start the next one until it's done. And here is the house rule for every reThought agent: no showings before the Zero to 45 meeting and a signed agreement." Pause. "I know. Some of you are already thinking 'but my buyers...' Remember your sealed card." [Pedro: tell them why you made this a house rule.]

slides.blockTitle: The buyer path and the first call
slides.visual: [Pedro: a photo that cues a buyer story, for example a car odometer or a stack of MLS printouts.]
slides.notes: [Pedro: tell a real story of a buyer you or an agent toured endlessly without a plan, and how it ended. Or one where the plan made it fast.]

slides.blockTitle: The buyer path and the first call
slides.visual: Six stepping stones crossing a stream.
slides.notes: "Before you dial, 60 seconds: what brought them in, is an alert on, do they own here. Then six steps, same order, every call. Every answer you give ends in a question. Say back their words. No 'how are you.' And motivation, own or rent, you never skip: it's the listing you might miss."

slides.blockTitle: The buyer path and the first call
slides.visual: A phone with a green call screen, "Maria · ad lead."
slides.notes: Volunteer plays Maria: rents, lease ends in five months, saw homes at an open house last weekend, needs financing help. Pedro runs all six steps start to finish in about three minutes. Room's job: "Count how many times I end with a question." Debrief: the number, and what they noticed about the recommendation.
slides.activity: Pedro and volunteer, 3 min; debrief 2 min.

slides.blockTitle: The buyer path and the first call
slides.visual: Left: a teacher's red pen. Right: an open hand.
slides.notes: "'Are you pre-approved?' sounds like a test they can fail. 'Would you like help with your financing options?' sounds like a friend. And if they signed with another agent, you respect it. Leave your name and number, and stop."

slides.blockTitle: The buyer path and the first call
slides.onScreen: "Run the call. All six steps. 5 minutes each."
slides.visual: Six small dots that light up one at a time. Timer 5:00.
slides.notes: "Partner A is the agent, B is the buyer. Buyer, make up a situation: own or rent, timeline, seen any homes. Agent runs all six steps with page 2 and 3 open. Then switch." Walk the room and listen for "how are you" and for anyone skipping motivation.

slides.blockTitle: The buyer path and the first call
slides.visual: A calm, confident person speaking, soft background.
slides.notes: "The appointment is a recommendation, not a request. Say it like a doctor, not like you're asking for a favor. Everybody, in English: 'Based on what you told me, here's what I recommend.' Now in Spanish." Room says both lines together. Then once to your partner, steady voice, with two times.
slides.activity: Whole room choral, then pairs, 2 min.

slides.visual: The words in a speech bubble, big, on a phone.
slides.notes: "Your buyer just said it. What do you usually say?" Take two honest answers ("Sure, what's your email?"). "And then what happens?" (Nothing.)

slides.visual: Three icons: a nodding head, a question mark, a two-slot calendar.
slides.notes: "Buyers stall four ways. Never argue, never hang up empty. Agree with them, ask one question, then offer two times." The four answers are on page 4.

slides.onScreen: "Stand. Partner fires stalls. You answer. Fast."
slides.visual: A ping-pong paddle and ball.
slides.notes: "Everyone up. Partner A fires the four stalls in any order, as fast as they want. Partner B answers each one: agree, ask, two times. 90 seconds, then switch."

slides.visual: A phone with a call timer still running, a green checkmark.
slides.notes: "Booked is not done. Eight more questions, and each one has a reason: how warm they are, the first homes to tour, no calls to other agents, every decision maker in the room, no lost buyers, a reply as a commitment, the listing appointment for owners, and catching the no-show now." Point to page 4; they'll use it in the role play.

slides.onScreen: "A practicar. Agent · Buyer · Scorer. 9 minutes a round."
slides.visual: Three chairs, two back to back, the third facing both. Timer 9:00, reset each round.
slides.notes: Merge pairs into threes. Use the buyer cards from the appendix. Each round: 1 minute for the buyer to read the card silently, 6 minutes for the call (Lessons 1 and 2, in order, phone timer on), 2 minutes to score: total, hidden facts found, one thing that worked, one fix by line number. No coaching mid-call. Rotate seats each round, new card. Pedro walks and listens; call out "two minutes left" each round. Goal: 14 of 20 and every hidden fact found. [Pedro: confirm the buyer cards are printed and in the appendix; if not, have three ready by table.]

slides.onScreen: "15 minutes a day. Text your score Friday."
slides.visual: A phone with a text: "Fri score: 16."
slides.notes: "Hands up if your third round was better than your first." Most will be. "That's 18 minutes of practice. Imagine 30 days. After the retreat: 15 minutes a day with your partner, text your total on Friday."

slides.blockTitle: The Zero to 45 meeting and the agreement
slides.onScreen: "What is your buyer most afraid of?"
slides.visual: A buyer at a kitchen table, head in hands, papers spread out.
slides.notes: "Tell your partner the fears you hear most. One minute." Then collect five on a flip chart. "Overpaying. Missing homes. The paperwork. Affording it. Something going wrong. The last agent disappearing. Every one of those is on page 6, with what you show them."

slides.blockTitle: The Zero to 45 meeting and the agreement
slides.onScreen: "One hour. They leave with four things."
slides.visual: A clock face divided into six colored slices, and four icons beside it: a phone (lender call), a search bar, a calendar, a signature.
slides.notes: "Diagnose first, then walk the map. Before they leave: lender call booked, search live on their phone, first tour on the calendar, agreement signed." Agenda timing is on page 6. Fair Housing: ask about the home and the commute, never about who will live there.

slides.blockTitle: The Zero to 45 meeting and the agreement
slides.onScreen: "I say the fear. You show the proof."
slides.visual: Two columns: a worried face, a green check.
slides.notes: Pedro reads a fear: "We're afraid we'll overpay." Pairs have 10 seconds to agree on which ONE benefit answers it, and say it in one sentence to each other. Do five fears. "Don't list twelve benefits. Answer the fear they told you."

slides.blockTitle: The Zero to 45 meeting and the agreement
slides.visual: A stopwatch, a signed paper beside it.
slides.notes: "That's how long the agreement takes when you explain it right. Four parts, plain words, pointing at the form."

slides.blockTitle: The Zero to 45 meeting and the agreement
slides.visual: In Milwaukee: an outline of Wisconsin. In Florida: an outline of Florida. One state per city, not both.
slides.notes: Milwaukee: walk the Wisconsin column, including the change starting January 1, 2027. Florida: walk the Florida column, transaction broker as default, disclosure timing. Both: the fee is a clear number, negotiable, never "whatever the seller pays." Upload the signed copy to Dashbrew the same day. [Pedro: confirm the current form names and versions with your compliance team before each retreat.]

slides.blockTitle: The Zero to 45 meeting and the agreement
slides.visual: Stopwatch counting up, large.
slides.notes: Hold up a real buyer agreement form for your state. Ask someone to time you. Do the four parts, pointing at each section as you say it. Then a volunteer fires one question from page 8; answer in one breath and go back to the form.

slides.blockTitle: The Zero to 45 meeting and the agreement
slides.visual: A form with a pen, a speech bubble. Timer 5:00, reset.
slides.notes: "Agent writes their 90-second version at the bottom of page 8 (2 minutes). Then: agent delivers it, partner times it and fires any three questions from the page. Agree, answer in one breath, back to the form, never argue about the paper. Switch." Spanish round if there's time: "Antes de ver casas..." from page 7.

slides.blockTitle: The Zero to 45 meeting and the agreement
slides.visual: Voice memo icon.
slides.notes: "Record your 90 seconds tonight and listen once. Where did you read instead of point?" Ask: "What's one question from page 8 you've been afraid of? Tell your partner your answer now." Bridge to break.

slides.blockTitle: The Zero to 45 meeting and the agreement
slides.visual: Countdown.
slides.notes: none.

slides.onScreen: "Your longest buyer saw how many homes?"
slides.visual: Car odometer spinning.
slides.notes: "Hands: 10? 20? 30 or more?" Laugh with whoever had the record. "More homes make a harder choice, not a better one."

slides.visual: A hand holding up a single key, other keys blurred on a table behind it.
slides.notes: "Brief them at the first door. After every house, same five questions, including 'what didn't you like,' even when they love it. Then: better or worse than the one we're keeping? Only one keeper." Ready signals on page 9: answer them right away.

slides.visual: A text bubble with a timer.
slides.notes: "Partner A tells B what happened on a made-up four-house tour. B gives the recap: today's keeper, what's off and why, the search update, the next tour time. Under 30 seconds. Switch." Remind: what they don't like narrows the search; never write down comments about who lives in an area.

slides.visual: Four levers on a control panel, all green.
slides.notes: "Win on more than price. Call the listing agent first. The six questions are on page 11. The best one: 'Besides price, what matters most to your seller?'" If they counter: answer within hours, not tomorrow. No personal letters or photos to sellers.

slides.onScreen: "You're the listing agent. Your partner calls."
slides.visual: Two phones, one labeled "listing agent."
slides.notes: "B plays a busy listing agent. A asks the six questions in order. B, give one useful hint only if they ask question 4 or 6 well. Switch."

slides.visual: A phone calendar with every Monday marked.
slides.notes: "Under contract, the dates rule. Each one is a task in the brew. The Monday call, every week, even with no news. Silence makes buyers nervous." Then: "And not ready is not a no. Stage them, keep the alert on, and when they come back, start the first call again from step one." Point to page 12.

slides.onScreen: "Your last real tour. Write the text now."
slides.visual: A phone keyboard, cursor blinking.
slides.notes: "Write the recap text you should have sent after your last real tour. If it's still useful, send it." Bridge: "Same promise, other side of the table: Listings."

slides.visual: A phone showing a contact list, one name glowing.
slides.notes: "Before you chase strangers: your next listing is probably already in your database. Who told you they own? Who bought from you three years ago?" Pairs: one name each, 1 minute.

slides.visual: Six small icons in a 2x3 grid: house with a tag, calendar, handshake, map pin, expired clock, "for sale" sign.
slides.notes: "Build six smart lists once in Dashbrew. Ten calls a day, oldest last contact first." Then the compliance line, clearly: scrub against Do Not Call every 31 days, call 8 to 8 owner's time, full name and reThought first, "stop" means removed today. In Florida, no more than three calls in 24 hours on the same subject, and texts count as calls. [Pedro: confirm any Wisconsin-specific calling rules for the Milwaukee version.]

slides.onScreen: "Page 1. Guess how many on each list."
slides.visual: Six blank number boxes.
slides.notes: "Estimate how many names you'd have on each of the six lists. Write the number next to each one. Total it. Divide by ten calls a day. That's how many days of calls are already sitting in your database." Ask for the biggest total in the room.

slides.visual: A front yard with an empty sign post, the sign removed.
slides.notes: "An expired is a seller who already decided to move. The listing ended, the plan didn't. Know the difference: expired, call it. Canceled, check the MLS first. Withdrawn, don't solicit. FSBO, a different call, earn trust." All four on page 2.

slides.visual: The word "EXPIRED" stamped in red, crossed out.
