slides.notes: "They've heard it from six agents today. Say: 'I noticed your home came off the market.' Everybody, in Spanish too." Room repeats the Spanish line from page 2.

slides.visual: [Pedro: a photo of an expired you relisted and sold, with the seller's OK, or the street.]
slides.notes: [Pedro: tell the story. Why it didn't sell the first time, what you asked on the first call, what you changed, the result.]

slides.visual: Three clock faces, the 8:00 one green.
slides.notes: "Pull the list at 7. Prep at 7:45: price history, days, photos, one thing you'd change. Dial at 8, not one minute before. Log every attempt the same day. The first call that sounds prepared gets the interview." Then the six moves of the expired call on page 3, which we'll run live in an hour. "You say a third of the words. They say the rest."

slides.onScreen: "Page 5. One real expired. Ten days. 7 minutes."
slides.visual: A ten-day calendar strip. Timer 7:00.
slides.notes: "Pull one expired from this morning's MLS on your phone, street only. Fill the plan: their deadline if you can guess it, your Day 3 door time, the monthly call date. Then glance at page 4: the eight things they'll say. We use them in the live round." Walk and help people find expireds in their MLS app.

slides.onScreen: "Leave the voicemail. Partner times it. Under 20."
slides.visual: Stopwatch at 0:20 in red.
slides.notes: "Use the voicemail on page 5, changed to your words. Say your number twice. Partner times it. Over 20 seconds, cut and redo." Then: "Put tomorrow at 7 AM on your calendar: your first expired morning."

slides.blockTitle: The call, the prep, the table
slides.visual: A price tag hanging off a doorknob, face down.
slides.notes: Take answers. "Last. Every answer earns the next question. One question, then listen. If you lead with price, you're a number. If you lead with their plan, you're the person who understood it."

slides.blockTitle: The call, the prep, the table
slides.visual: A five-rung ladder, a small figure stepping down one rung, green.
slides.notes: "They say no to the appointment? Don't hang up. Step down one rung: a 20-minute walk-through, then a prep guide, then a market update, then their date. Never jump two. Write the rung in Dashbrew before you dial the next number."

slides.blockTitle: The call, the prep, the table
slides.onScreen: "Partner says no. You step down. Every time."
slides.visual: The ladder with a red "NO" at each rung.
slides.notes: "A plays a seller who says no to everything until rung 4 or 5. B steps down one rung at a time, using page 6. Two minutes, then switch."

slides.blockTitle: The call, the prep, the table
slides.visual: Car keys and a folded paper on a passenger seat.
slides.notes: "A real seller says yes to all three asks: the mortgage statement, the key, a photo date. Fewer? Keep them on the ladder. Walk the home before you decide go or not yet. Disclosures are the seller's own answers. Never coach them."

slides.blockTitle: The call, the prep, the table
slides.visual: A yellow legal pad with three handwritten items, each crossed off with a green pen.
slides.notes: "At the table, ask their three things and write them on a pad. Then show only the pieces of the plan that answer those three, and cross each one off. It's a consultation, not a presentation. Thirty minutes, eight stops, same order." The stops and the "not yet" lines are on page 8. [Pedro: show your real #reElevated Marketing Plan cover here, or hold it up.]

slides.blockTitle: The call, the prep, the table
slides.visual: The number huge, a calendar with six pages flying off.
slides.notes: "That's the sample on page 9: $4,000 a month in mortgage, taxes, insurance and utilities, times six months sitting. Gone. Waiting has a price. Show them their own monthly bill, not a lecture."

slides.blockTitle: The call, the prep, the table
slides.visual: A made-up walk-away sheet (sample numbers): Sale price $415,000 · Payoff −$236,000 · Fee: as agreed in writing · Closing costs −$5,200 · Taxes prorated −$3,100 · "What you walk away with" in green, blank for the fee line.
slides.notes: "Sellers don't spend the price. They spend what they walk away with. Their payoff comes from their own statement, that's why you asked for it. Never quote a 'usual' fee rate. It's whatever you agree in writing."

slides.blockTitle: The call, the prep, the table
slides.onScreen: "Seller names a price. You ask how."
slides.visual: A speech bubble with a question mark and a dollar sign.
slides.notes: "Seller says a number 10% too high. Agent: 'How did you land on that number? Help me understand.' Then listen. Then the what-if question from page 9. Never argue. 3 minutes each." Before switching, everyone says the plan question from page 10 in Spanish: "¿Esperamos a que lo encuentren, o salimos a buscarlos?"
slides.activity: Pairs, 3 min each, choral Spanish line.

slides.blockTitle: The call, the prep, the table
slides.visual: Two signatures on a single line, one agent, one seller.
slides.notes: "Sellers fear one thing more than a low offer: an agent who disappears. Take that fear off the table in writing. Feedback the day it comes in, a real call every five days, and if you don't keep it, they can let you go." Ask: "Who in this room is ready to sign that promise on every listing in 2027?" Hands. "Then prove it every week with the call log and the ad results." Then a quick pair: say the guarantee to your partner in your own words, both languages if you can.

slides.blockTitle: The expired call, live, in threes
slides.visual: Three chairs in a triangle.
slides.notes: "New threes, people you haven't practiced with today. The seller reads the card on page 13 silently. The coach reads it out loud only after the round. Coach gives one fix only."

slides.blockTitle: The expired call, live, in threes
slides.visual: Timer 8:00, phone icon.
slides.notes: Pedro calls time at 4 minutes and 1 minute. After the call: 2 minutes to score Round 1 on page 14, goal 14 of 20. Coach gives one fix. Rotate seats.

slides.blockTitle: The expired call, live, in threes
slides.visual: Timer 8:00, a kitchen table icon.
slides.notes: "Same three people, new seats. Dana wants to relist at her old price. The CMA says lower. Let her say the number first, ask how she landed on it, show the walk-away and the cost of waiting, set the 30-day check-in." Score Round 2, goal 7 of 10. Rotate.

slides.blockTitle: The expired call, live, in threes
slides.visual: Timer 8:00.
slides.notes: "Third person runs the call this time. Everyone has now been agent once." Score it. Coach gives one fix.

slides.blockTitle: The expired call, live, in threes
slides.visual: A single green wrench.
slides.notes: "Write your one fix on page 14. Then each person says it to their three." Take two to the room. Remind: after every real appointment, send the credentials email the same day, and every seller lands in one of the stages at the bottom of page 13.

slides.visual: The number huge, a small Wisconsin outline (Milwaukee) or a question mark over a Florida outline (Florida).
slides.notes: Milwaukee: "In Wisconsin, it's on the MLS within 48 hours of signing, from midnight of the contract date. Weekends count." Florida: "Here, each MLS sets its own deadline and coming-soon rules. Ask me before you promise a seller a date." Both: marketed in public means it goes in the MLS within about a business day. [Pedro: confirm your Florida MLS rule for the slide.]

slides.visual: Four steps on a timeline: Day 0, 48 hours, Day 2 to 5, Launch day.
slides.notes: "Photo day isn't listing day. Pro photos take a few days, and you use them to get every room ready. Walk it at signing with your phone; those photos become the seller's prep list. Built in Dashbrew as tasks so nothing slips."

slides.visual: A clipboard with lines, a calendar icon. Timer 5:00.
slides.notes: "Pick a current or recent listing, or your own home. Interior, exterior, community: every feature with a year, amenities with drive times. Then AI writes the remarks and you check every word. Describe the home, never who should live there."

slides.visual: Left: a phone with "um, nothing new..." Right: a phone with a small chart.
slides.notes: "No feedback in 24 hours? Call the agent and ask what their buyer would pay. Every five days, a real call: showings, feedback, ad results, new comps. And every listing is a sign: post it everywhere, after it's on the MLS, with the seller's OK."

slides.visual: A real pie cut into four, overhead shot, warm light.
slides.notes: "Two days, one page. A real estate business runs on four slices. Miss one and it stalls. Every lesson you learned this week fed one of them."

slides.visual: The pie as a clean diagram, four labeled slices, "You" in a green circle at the center.
slides.notes: "Center is you: identity and mindset. You set it once. Sales and marketing grow the pie. Admin and accountability keep it. Page 1 shows which lesson feeds which slice." Ask: "Which slice did you think about the least before this week?"

slides.visual: The four labels in the screen corners, matching the room corners (reuse the corner signs from El motor, relabeled).
slides.notes: "Go stand in the corner of the slice that's weakest for you right now." Look at the room. "Talk to the people in your corner: what's the one thing that would fix it? Two minutes." Then one person per corner shares.
slides.activity: Whole room moves, corner groups 3 min, 4 shares.

slides.onScreen: "Page 2. Shade it. One fix per slice. 6 minutes."
slides.visual: An unshaded pie with a green marker beside it. Timer 6:00.
slides.notes: "Shade each slice 1 to 5: how strong is it today? A lopsided pie shows where to start. Then one fix per slice, one line each." Remind: "You'll shade this same pie again on March 31."

slides.visual: A January calendar page with four colored rows.
slides.notes: "The year gets won in the first 90 days. Fill January first: your lead gen block, your storefront and ads, your Dashbrew sort, your Monday planning report. Then your own row at the bottom. February and March, tonight." Partners swap and read each other's January.

slides.visual: A compass, the four slice names at N, E, S, W.
slides.notes: Read problems from page 4, out of order, in your own words: "My leads go cold." "Buyers meet me but don't sign." "I'm busy all week and my numbers are flat." "I lost my why." Room shouts the slice, then someone shouts the lesson to go back to. "Keep this book on your desk. Same problem two weeks in a row? Bring the page to me. We fix it together."

slides.visual: The box from Day 1 morning, lid open, cards inside.
slides.notes: "Yesterday at 9 AM you wrote the sentence that keeps you from trying new things. Come get it." Everyone walks up to collect their own card. (Have a helper spread them on a table so it moves quickly.)
slides.activity: Whole room walks to collect cards, 3 min.

slides.visual: The card, unfolded, on a table, blurry handwriting.
slides.notes: "Open it. Read it to yourself. After two days, is that sentence still true? Under it, write the open-mind question you'll ask instead. Something like: 'How will I make this work here?'" Silent 2 minutes. Then: "If you're willing, read the old sentence and the new question to your partner." Ask two brave volunteers to read to the room. [Pedro: read your own Day 1 sealed sentence first, to go first.]
slides.activity: Individual 2 min, pairs 2 min, two volunteers.

slides.visual: A pen on a signature line, green ink.
slides.notes: "Turn to the commitment card in the appendix. Write your one line for 2027 from page 14 of Open the Mind, your one fix per slice from the recap, and sign it. Your partner signs as witness." [Pedro: confirm the commitment card page number in the appendix; it was not in the condensed files.]

slides.visual: Two calendar pages, both circled in green.
slides.notes: "Two dates in your phone now. Friday, January 8: your first Friday score, texted to your partner. March 31: we rescore the pie together. The slice that grew the least picks your next 90 days." [Pedro: confirm the follow-up plan: who runs the Monday planning reports, any monthly check-in, and the March 31 session format (in office or Zoom).]
slides.workbook: Recap p.3 (March 31), Open the Mind p.16 (Friday score)

slides.notes: Don't put your note on the screen; say it. Speak from the heart, about why you built reThought, what you see in this room, and what "together" means to you.
